transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

The first suspect is restricted airflow rather than a failed part: on a condenser dryer, fluff in the door filter or lower condenser area can make drying take hours. A poor washer spin, an overfull drum, or a low-heat/short programme can do the same. If the airflow is clean but it is genuinely cold, then a heater or thermal protection fault becomes more likely. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Clean the fluff filter in the door opening thoroughly, including the filter housing. Wash the filter if it has a fine film on it, then let it dry before refitting. A blocked filter restricts airflow. 2. Open the lower front flap and remove/clean the condenser or lower filter assembly as applicable. Rinse removable parts under the tap, remove visible fluff, and refit only when they are drip-dry. This is the most useful check for a condenser dryer. 3. Check the next load is no more than about two-thirds of the drum and has been well spun in the washing machine. Use a normal Cotton/Extra Dry-type programme rather than a short, delicate or low-dryness setting. 4. After reassembly, run a normal programme for 10–15 minutes and check whether the air inside feels clearly warm when you open the door. If it is warm, the issue is more likely airflow, loading, programme choice or moisture sensing. If it is still cold, stop there and arrange an engineer: on this type of dryer the heater/thermal cut-out circuit would need diagnosis after the airflow has been cleaned. Do not dismantle panels or test electrical parts yourself. Is it clearly warming after 10–15 minutes once the filters/lower section have been cleaned?

Cleaned the door filter (waxy film, needed a scrub) and the condenser, which was matted with lint. Before that, it was hot inside the drum after 20 min. Test cycle after cleaning is done, so can I tell you how it went?

Yes — please do. The waxy door-filter film and matted condenser could very plausibly have been the main restriction, especially as the drum was getting hot before cleaning. Tell me whether the test load was dry, improved but still damp, or no better, and whether the programme finished normally or ended unusually early. That will separate a remaining airflow/load issue from a possible moisture-sensing problem.
Much better. Clothes dried in about 100 minutes and the water container was nearly full. Programme finished normally.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That looks resolved. The dryer was heating, it now dries the load in about 100 minutes, collected plenty of water and completed normally — all of that points to the wax-coated filter and lint-matted condenser restricting airflow, rather than a failed heater or sensor. To prevent it returning: clean the door filter after every load, and periodically wash it to remove the invisible fabric-conditioner film; clean the condenser/lower area regularly too. Avoid refitting parts until they are drip-dry. No part replacement or engineer is indicated at this point.

candidates: Restricted airflow from lint filter or condenser/heat-exchanger blockage (high)
Laundry entering very wet, excessive load, or unsuitable programme/dryness setting (medium)
Weak or absent heating, such as heater/thermal protection fault (low)
